dynamicSlides.title: Most BFSI platforms are functionally strong, but experience-poor.
What BFSI institutions actually want from digital platforms
dynamicSlides.leftText:
Transactions work
Customers can transact, but
feature depth and daily usage
often remain lower than
expected.
Journeys are
fragmented
Onboarding, servicing,
payments, investments, and
support often feel like separate
systems.
Digital servicing still
leaks
Users fall back to RM, branch,
dynamicSlides.rightText:
call center, or assisted channels
for clarity and completion.
Interfaces expect effort
Many platforms still depend on
users figuring out what to do,
when to do it, and why it matters.
The result
•
Digital investment rises, but usage, trust, and self-serve behaviour do not scale proportionately.
•
Product teams add features, while customers still struggle with confidence, clarity, and completion.
•
The platform remains transactional, instead of becoming a trusted decision and servicing layer.

dynamicSlides.title: What this now demands from the platform
dynamicSlides.tagline: When the business outcome changes, the platform has to change. And when the platform has to change, the way it is designed and built must change too.
dynamicSlides.leftText:
is friction.
•

•
Legacy architecture and backend constraints
that limit structural change
•
Feature-heavy interfaces with low clarity and
high cognitive load
•
Compliance, security, and trust requirements
that increase complexity
•
Data-rich platforms that show information but
do not guide action
dynamicSlides.rightText:

•

•
Unclear next steps in onboarding and
servicing journeys
•

•
Digital channels that still feel less
trustworthy than human assistance

rows.title: CLEARER
rows.body: Information hierarchy, language, and flows must reduce uncertainty and mental effort.

rows.title: MORE TRUST-BUILDING
rows.body: Journeys must reinforce confidence through transparency, reassurance, and contextual clarity.

rows.title: MORE TASK-ORIENTED
rows.body: Users should be able to complete financial actions quickly, not navigate product silos.

rows.title: DECISION-SUPPORTIVE
rows.body: The platform should help users know what matters, what to do next, and why.

rows.title: ADAPTIVE
rows.body: Different users, goals, and moments should trigger different guidance, prompts, and surfaces.

rows.title: EASIER TO EVOLVE
rows.body: Improvements must be testable and phased within enterprise constraints, not only through big-bang rewrites.

dynamicSlides.title: BEAM: a practical model for behavior-aware banking experiences
dynamicSlides.tagline: A simple framework for turning signals into useful actions inside the platform.

rows.title: B
rows.body: Behaviour

rows.title: • Capture user actions, habits, drop-offs, and transaction patterns across journeys.
rows.body: E

rows.title: Evaluation
rows.body: • Interpret what those signals mean in context: intent, hesitation, risk, or opportunity.

rows.title: A
rows.body: Action

rows.title: • Trigger timely prompts, nudges, prioritisation, assistance, or adaptive flows inside the product.
rows.body: M

rows.title: Measurement
rows.body: • Track whether the intervention improved completion, adoption, servicing efficiency, or usage.

rows.title: Illustrative use cases
rows.body:
• Repeated bill payment behaviour -> surface autopay setup
• Failed onboarding patterns -> simplify or route to assisted completion
• Dormant savings behaviour -> surface goal or investment nudges
• Underused salary account benefits -> highlight relevant tools and actions
